description: Check a completion handback against the repository's own record, before you say done. Give exactly one subject: a GitHub pull request (repository owner/name and pullRequest), or a GitLab merge request (gitlabProject, the project's full path, and mergeRequest, its iid; gitlabHost for a host other than gitlab.com; GitLab profile). Members of both, of neither, or part of one are an input error. Then give exactly one of: block, the dunstan-handback block as a JSON object; or report, the report text that carries exactly one ```dunstan-handback fence. Of the checks claims, checks.allSucceeded is true only if every counted check run concluded success, so a skipped or neutral run makes it false; checks.noneFailed is true if none concluded other than success, skipped or neutral and at least one succeeded. Returns the verdict (pass, fail or unverifiable), the claims table, and the full record as JSON. Same checker and same verdict as `dunstan check` on the same evidence; no model decides. Reads GitHub metadata with GITHUB_TOKEN for a pull request, GitLab metadata with GITLAB_TOKEN for a merge request (each token goes only to its own forge's host; without GITLAB_TOKEN a GitLab tests claim is unverifiable, even on a public project), and writes nothing to the forge or the repository; the record is written to a file only when you pass outPath. If the verdict is not pass, report the rows as they are; change the work, not the block.

block.description: The dunstan-handback block as a JSON object. Give this or report, not both.

gitlabHost.description: A GitLab subject: the GitLab host name, such as gitlab.example.com. Absent: gitlab.com.

gitlabProject.description: A GitLab subject: the project's full path, group/subgroup/.../project, with mergeRequest. Read with GITLAB_TOKEN. Give this subject or the GitHub one, not both.

mergeRequest.description: A GitLab subject: the merge request's iid, the number after ! (a positive integer).

outPath.description: Write the record to this path (must not exist). Without it nothing is written.

pullRequest.description: A GitHub subject: the pull request number the handback is about.

report.description: The report text, carrying exactly one ```dunstan-handback fence. Give this or block, not both.

repository.description: A GitHub subject: the repository, owner/name, with pullRequest. Read with GITHUB_TOKEN. Give this subject or the GitLab one, not both.

testPaths.description: Optional, GitHub only (DRAFT): the file patterns the user counts as tests, such as *_test.go or src/**/*.test.ts (a pattern without / matches a file name in any directory). The table then lists each changed test file as context, and the record keeps the patterns. They never change the verdict. You may propose them from the repository's test runners and layout, but pass only patterns the user has accepted: they are the user's statement of what a test is, not yours.

name: dunstan_check_handback
title: Check a handback against the record
